newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Energy Dept seeks comments on SPR's future.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Energy Dept seeks comments on SPR's future.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department said it would seek public comment for the next 45 days to help it determine whether the nation should keep the Strategic Oil Reserve, and how it should be operated.

The department said it wants views on whether the country should keep the reserve, what its size should be, how the oil should be distributed, and on whether it is appropriate to sell oil from the reserve to generate revenue.
The reserve was established in 1975 as a tool to try to ensure energy security in case of another supply disruption such as the 1973 oil embargo.
The reserve reached a peak of 592 million barrels in 1994, but about 28 million barrels have been sold since early last year to raise government revenues.

The current supply equals about 67 days of net oil imports, and the United States relies on a combination of the reserve and private stocks to meet its international obligations with allies to maintain supplies in case of emergencies.
The Energy Department is reviewing overall policies of the SPR, particularly since it has been tapped in the last year as a revenue source to help reduce the budget deficit.
